title: 3D viewport material drop tooltip shows "Hold Command" on macOS, but should say "Hold Control"
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.7.2.stable.official (`ed1daf0bf`).
- Also observed in Godot 4.7.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.6.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 Pro - Apple M4 Pro (12 threads) - 48.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When dragging a texture or material from the FileSystem dock onto a `MeshInstance3D` in the 3D viewport, the hover tooltip on macOS says to "Hold Command" to apply it as a surface material override. In reality the Control key on MacOS triggers material slot override, not the Command key.

Screenshot:
https://www.pasteboard.co/4pRumPdjPh9_.png

In my testing:

- A normal drop assigns the material to `GeometryInstance3D > Geometry > Material Override`.
- Holding Cmd produces the same whole-object material override.
- Holding the Control key instead assigns it to `MeshInstance3D > Surface Material Override`.

The tooltip and recognized modifier should agree. Either the tooltip should identify Control, or Cmd should activate the surface-override behavior.

The behavior appears consistent with `_apply_preview_material()` checking `Key::CTRL`, while the tooltip formats the modifier using `CMD_OR_CTRL`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a blank Godot project with no editor plugins, GDExtensions, or custom engine modules.
2. Create a 3D scene.
3. Add a `MeshInstance3D`.
4. Assign it a built-in `BoxMesh`.
5. Drag `icon.svg`, a texture, or a saved material from the FileSystem dock over the box.
6. Observe that the viewport tooltip says to hold Cmd for a surface material override.
7. Hold Cmd and drop the resource.
8. Select the `MeshInstance3D` and observe that `GeometryInstance3D > Geometry > Material Override` was assigned.
9. Undo or clear that override.
10. Repeat the drop while holding the physical Control key.
11. Observe that `MeshInstance3D > Surface Material Override > 0` was assigned instead.

Note that a  BoxMesh has only one mesh surface, so both results look identical on all six sides. The difference is visible in the Inspector properties described above. A mesh with multiple surfaces can also be used to make the difference visually apparent.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

A newly created blank project is sufficient. No scripts or third-party plugins are required.
